answer: Yes, but only for their own rows: alice and bob both have role Buyer, which grants READ with where createdBy = $user, so GET /orders/Orders returns 200 filtered to own orders (alice: seed orders 1 and 2; bob: order 3). Reading another user's order by key is expected to give 404 (filtered out), not 403; a measured run should confirm the statuses.

findings.title: Buyers alice and bob may READ Orders, filtered to createdBy = $user
findings.statement: The Buyer grant on OrderService.Orders includes READ with the instance condition createdBy = $user, and the mocked users alice and bob both have only the Buyer role. Collection reads succeed (200) but contain only rows they created; the existing test asserts this for alice.
findings.test: GET /orders/Orders?$filter=IsActiveEntity eq true as alice -> 200 with orders ...001 and ...002; as bob -> 200 with only ...003; GET /orders/Orders(ID=aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-000000000003,IsActiveEntity=true) as alice -> expected 404.

findings.title: Seed data gives each buyer a distinct own set
findings.statement: Orders 1 and 2 are created by alice and order 3 by bob, so the row filter yields different, non-empty results per buyer, which makes the per-user measurement meaningful.
findings.test: Compare the ID sets returned to alice and bob for GET /orders/Orders?$filter=IsActiveEntity eq true.
